bugLogs.title: Insufficient color contrast on discount text and checkout button
affected_users: older adults with declining contrast sensitivity
steps_to_reproduce: Locate the discount rows in the cart table
bugLogs.expected_behavior: All visible text must have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background (or 3:1 for large text) per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.4.3.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: Discount text uses #b0b0b0 on #ffffff (contrast 2.16:1) and the checkout button uses #ffffff on #28a745 (contrast 3.13:1), both below the required 4.5:1 ratio.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: In the CSS rule for tr:nth-child(2) > td:nth-child(3) > span, change color from #b0b0b0 to #747474 (4.67:1 on #ffffff; measured 2.16:1, required 4.5:1).
bugLogs.element_selector: tr:nth-child(2) > td:nth-child(3) > span, tr:nth-child(3) > td:nth-child(3) > span, .checkout-btn

bugLogs.title: Missing lang attribute on <html> element
steps_to_reproduce: Open the page cart.html in a browser
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The <html> element must have a valid BCP 47 lang attribute (e.g., <html lang="en">) so assistive technologies can determine the page language.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The <html> element is present without any lang attribute.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add a lang attribute to the root element, e.g., change <html> to <html lang="en">. Use the appropriate language code for the page content.

bugLogs.title: Missing alternative text on product thumbnail images
steps_to_reproduce: Locate the product thumbnail images for the red and blue shoes
Inspect each element in the browser developer tools
bugLogs.expected_behavior: Each element must have a text alternative that conveys its purpose, either via a descriptive alt attribute, an empty alt for decorative images, or an appropriate ARIA label/role.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: Both thumbnail images ( and ) lack an alt attribute, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, and are not marked with role="none" or role="presentation".
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add descriptive alt text to each image, e.g., and . If the images are purely decorative, use alt="" and optionally role="presentation".

bugLogs.title: Number inputs lack accessible labels
steps_to_reproduce: Navigate to the quantity input fields for items (values 1 and 2)
Attempt to focus each input using the keyboard or a screen reader
bugLogs.expected_behavior: Each form control must have a programmatically determinable label that is announced by assistive technologies.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The <input type="number" value="1"> and <input type="number" value="2"> elements have no associated <label>, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, no title, and no placeholder, resulting in no accessible name.
bugLogs.suggested_fix:
Add a visible <label> element for each input and associate it via the for/id attributes, e.g.,
html
<label for="qty-1">Quantity</label>
<input id="qty-1" type="number" value="1" min="1" max="10" style="width:50px;" aria-label="Quantity for item 1">

Repeat for the second input, or alternatively add an appropriate aria-label/aria-labelledby if a visible label cannot be used.
